verified_facts.text: Spirit explored Gusev Crater and searched rocks and soil for clues about past water.
Spirit found a patch rich in silica, a clue that may point to ancient hot-water activity.
Spirit was sent to explore rocks and soil for clues about whether water once changed Mars.
Spirit launched June 10, 2003, and landed in Gusev Crater on January 3, 2004.
Spirit used cameras, spectrometers, a microscope, magnets, and a rock-abrasion tool to study its surroundings.
Spirit worked on Mars for more than six years, far beyond its planned 90-day primary mission.

verified_facts.text: Opportunity explored Meridiani Planum, where it found tiny hematite-rich spheres nicknamed blueberries.
The rocks and hematite-rich spheres studied by Opportunity provided evidence that liquid water once affected this region.
NASA reports that Opportunity drove 45.16 kilometers during its mission.
Opportunity searched Martian rocks and soil for evidence of past water and environments that could have supported life.
Opportunity used cameras, spectrometers, a microscope, magnets, and a rock-abrasion tool to examine the Martian surface.
Opportunity last communicated on June 10, 2018. NASA declared the mission ended on February 13, 2019.
Opportunity operated on Mars for almost 15 years and traveled 45.16 kilometers, according to NASA’s mission profile.

verified_nssdca_facts.text: The Mars Pathfinder lander reached Mars on July 4, 1997. Sojourner rolled onto the surface on July 6.
Sojourner had six wheels. An operator on Earth drove it using images from the rover and lander.
Radio signals took about 10 minutes to travel between Earth and Mars, so Sojourner needed some ability to act on its own while waiting.
Sojourner's first planned goals covered its first 7 Mars days, within about 10 meters of the lander.

key_findings: Completed the first powered, controlled flight on another planet on 2021-04-19.
Completed 72 flights; the final flight was 2024-01-18.

verified_facts.text: On April 19, 2021, Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.
Ingenuity completed 72 flights. Its final flight was January 18, 2024; NASA announced the mission end on January 25.
Ingenuity was built to test whether powered, controlled flight could work in Mars’s thin atmosphere.
Ingenuity carried a color terrain camera and a black-and-white navigation camera; it was a technology demonstration, not a rover.
Ingenuity arrived with Perseverance in February 2021, made its first flight on April 19, 2021, and its final flight on January 18, 2024.
After its flight test succeeded, Ingenuity also helped the Perseverance team scout routes from the air.

verified_facts.text: Surveyor 3 used a surface sampler to dig four trenches, perform four bearing tests, and make thirteen impact tests.
Apollo 12 astronauts visited Surveyor 3 in 1969 and returned its soil scoop and television camera for study.
Surveyor 3 tested a soft landing and investigated the Moon’s surface and soil.
Surveyor 3 used a television camera and a surface sampler to examine the lunar ground.
Surveyor 3 landed on April 20, 1967, and last communicated on May 4, 1967. Apollo 12 astronauts visited it in 1969.
Apollo 12 returned Surveyor 3’s soil scoop and television camera so scientists could study them on Earth.

verified_facts.text: The Apollo 17 lunar rover was used on three traverses and covered 35.9 kilometers in total.
Apollo 17’s longest single traverse was 20.1 kilometers. Its maximum distance from the lunar module was 7.6 kilometers.
The Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle helped astronauts explore more of the lunar surface during their mission.
The LRV was a crewed, battery-powered electric vehicle designed to carry astronauts and equipment across the Moon.
Apollo 17 astronauts used the lunar rover on three surface traverses.
The Apollo 17 rover covered 35.9 kilometers in total; its longest traverse was 20.1 kilometers, and its maximum range from the lunar module was 7.6 kilometers.
